newsitem.title: UK: SEP Industrial down after cautious statement.
newsitem.headline: SEP Industrial down after cautious statement.

text.p: Shares in Britain's SEP Industrial Holdings Plc fell on Wednesday after the industrial fasteners, electrical and auto components group posted an eight percent profit rise but warned of tough trading in its distribution unit.
At 1330 GMT the stock was down 8-3/4p or 17.5 percent to 41-1/4p, after earlier touching a 21-month low of 39p.

"Overall trading conditions in the distribution division continue to deteriorate against a background of weak demand, de-stocking and pressure on sales price levels," said chairman and chief executive Paul Formby.

He said overall results for 1997 were extremely difficult to predict, as the strong contribution expected from the manufacturing and logistics divisions could be cancelled out by continued weakness at its Jaton unit.
Formby said the company was taking action to reduce both operating and bought-in costs and said a reorganisation of distribution methods was expected to enable considerable savings to be made.
Pre-tax profits in the year ended September 30 rose 8.0 percent to 5.95 million stg on sales which rose to 56.2 million stg from 54.71 million.
The dividend was raised 9.4 percent to 1.75p.
